questions.prompt: Explain how Ramp turns an answer into a review rating and a mastery number, and why the roadmap going green is meant to be trustworthy.

keyPoints.text: The rating comes from correctness, time relative to the expected time, and hint use.
keyPoints.quote: The rating is derived from whether you were right, how long you took relative to the question's expected time, and whether you used a hint

keyPoints.text: Explain items are the exception: the learner rates them.
keyPoints.quote: except for `explain` items, which you rate yourself.

keyPoints.text: Any correct answer earns a 40% floor.
keyPoints.quote: answering correctly at all earns a floor of 40%

keyPoints.text: The rest of mastery comes from stability, which only grows through successful reviews.
keyPoints.quote: the rest comes from FSRS stability, which only grows through successful reviews.

keyPoints.text: Mastery fades while a review is overdue, so green means you would still know it later.
keyPoints.quote: It then fades while a review is overdue — so the roadmap going green means you'd still know it next month

questions.prompt: Describe the seven question formats and how each one's answer is shaped in the content files.

keyPoints.text: mcq has a single correct choice; its answer is a choice index.
multi selects all that apply with partial credit; its answer is an array of indices.
predict compares output text with whitespace and quote style ignored.
keyPoints.quote: "What does this log?" — free text, whitespace and quote style ignored

keyPoints.text: fill blanks may accept alternatives separated by a pipe.
explain items need keywords and a model answer instead of an answer.
code items need starter code, a solution and test cases.

questions.prompt: Explain the authoring rules and checks that keep the question bank and learners' schedules consistent.

keyPoints.text: Content is one JSON file per track, re-seeded after edits.
Ids come from track, module and position.
keyPoints.quote: Item ids are derived from the track slug, module slug and position

keyPoints.text: So edits and appends keep schedules intact.
keyPoints.quote: editing an explanation or appending a question leaves everyone's review schedule intact.

keyPoints.text: Reordering or removing changes ids and loses history.
keyPoints.quote: Reordering or removing items changes ids

keyPoints.text: check:gradable feeds each item its own answer and asserts the grader agrees.
keyPoints.quote: feeds every item its own answer and asserts the grader agrees

keyPoints.text: It catches answers past the choices, untypeable fills and predicts the normaliser rejects.
keyPoints.quote: it catches an answer index pointing past the end of the choices

keyPoints.text: The sandbox is a worker so a runaway loop can be killed.
keyPoints.quote: The code sandbox (a worker, so a runaway loop can be killed)
